identity.title: A Comprehensive Dust Model Applied to the Resolved Beta Pictoris Debris Disk from Optical to Radio Wavelengths

paper_type_evidence.quote: We model five images of the $\beta$ Pictoris disk: two in scattered light from *HST*/STIS at 0.58 $\ensuremath{\mu}m$ and *HST*/WFC3 at 1.16 $\ensuremath{\mu}m$
We used the ALMA 870 $\ensuremath{\mu}m$ continuum image previously published by (cite: dent2014).

question.value: Can varying the dust composition (optical constants) let a single model fit both thermal emission and scattered light of the beta Pic debris disk?

evidence.quote: We investigate whether varying the dust composition (described by the optical constants) can solve a persistent problem in debris disk modeling—the inability to fit the thermal emission without over-predicting the scattered light.
We used the ALMA 870 $\ensuremath{\mu}m$ continuum image previously published by (cite: dent2014).

method.value: Rotate images to align the disk mid-plane, take a strip along the mid-plane and average the pixels, separately for the NE and SW sides

evidence.quote: We extracted radial profiles by selecting a strip of each image along the mid-plane of the disk and computed the mean value of the pixels at each point along the length of the strip.
5 pixels (0.5$''$) for the STIS, WFC3, MIPS, PACS, and ALMA images, respectively

analysis_steps.goal: Fit spatial parameters of the parent body belt to ALMA

method.value: Grid search over r_in, r_out, p and amplitude with chi-squared on the radial profile

evidence.quote: We performed this fit with a grid search across the parameters of interest
We generated models with $r_\text{in}$ ranging from 35 to 70 au, $r_\text{out}$ from 130 to 170 au, and $p$ from 0 to 2.0.

assumptions.value: Fixed a_min 5 micron, a_max 5000 micron, q=3.65, astronomical silicates; 4 deg half-opening wedge, edge-on

evidence.quote: the grain properties were fixed at $a_\text{min}$ = 5 $\ensuremath{\mu}m$, $a_\text{max}$ = 5000 $\ensuremath{\mu}m$, $q$ = 3.65
We performed this fit with a grid search across the parameters of interest, and the results are shown in red in Figure [8](#fig:SpatialConstraints).

validation.value: Agrees with Dent et al. 2014 annuli modeling

evidence.quote: Our values of $r_\text{in}$ and $r_\text{out}$ agree well with the analysis by (cite: dent2014)

method.value: Fit WFC3 profile at r>8" for halo p; PACS for halo r_out

evidence.quote: To measure $p$, we used the WFC3 data

validation.value: Checked against alpha=-p-1 relation of Strubbe & Chiang 2006

evidence.quote: predicted $p$ values of 2.5 and 3.0 for the NE and SW sides, which agreed with what we found from model fitting

analysis_steps.goal: Fit grain sizes and composition to all five images simultaneously

method.value: Grid search chi-squared per image, normalized by each image's minimum and averaged; fit r>3" on NE side; models with 100% astrosil, generic optical constants, and four-material Bruggeman mixture

evidence.quote: We normalized the matrix from each image by the $\chi^2$ value of the best fitting model to that image in an attempt to weight the contribution from each of the five images equally.

assumptions.value: Densities 2.7, 1.2, 1.8 g/cm3 for silicate, ice, organics

evidence.quote: The grain densities were 2.7 g/cm$^3$ for the astronomical silicates (as is commonly assumed), and 1.2 and 1.8 g/cm$^3$ for the ice and organics
We performed our fitting with a grid search, populating a chi-squared matrix for each of the five images, with one dimension of the matrix for each free parameter.

validation.value: Checked against SED, SW side, T-ReCS profiles and scattered light colors

evidence.quote: In all three cases, our model agrees satisfactorily with the additional data set.

used_for.value: Generating model images in thermal emission and scattered light

evidence.quote: We used the code `dustmap` v.3.1.1 (cite: stark2011) to generate model disk images

evidence.quote: we performed the convolution of the two images with MATLAB’s `conv2` function

findings_qualitative.value: Pure astronomical silicates cannot fit both thermal and scattered light; silicate+organic mix does, with little ice or vacuum

evidence.quote: We achieve a good fit to all datasets with grains composed predominantly of silicates and organics, while ice and vacuum are, at most, present in small amounts.

claims.hypothesis: Astronomical silicates alone can fit thermal and scattered light
claims.experiment: Grid fit of five radial profiles
claims.result: Model too faint at MIPS/PACS, too bright at STIS

evidence.quote: this model did not achieve a good fit to all of the images
We found that a mixture of silicates and organics was preferred, while water ice and vacuum were not favored.

claims.hypothesis: Sub-blowout grains are needed in the halo

evidence.quote: We could not achieve a good fit to the data with any grain composition, confirming that sub-blowout grains were a necessary part of our model.

limitations_admitted.value: Fit only to NE side; SW side fit imperfectly at 70 micron

evidence.quote: the halo component under-predicts the observed flux at 70 $\ensuremath{\mu}m$

referee_caveats_inferred: Grid search with coarse steps gives no formal uncertainties
Composition degenerate among material choices; only one optical-constant set tested

missing_for_reproduction: Reduced ALMA image (obtained from Dent et al.)
Tabulated optical constants of the best model are only partly printed
reproducibility.score_reason: Modeling recipe is detailed but ALMA data are an inherited image and dustmap needed.
